meal.title: OS Regaining CPU Control
meal.objective: Identify the challenges the OS faces when it must take back the CPU

voice.script: What happens when the OS needs to yank the CPU away? Imagine a process happily running. The OS can only step in at special moments because normal code runs without special rights. How does the OS regain control from a running process? It relies on privileged mechanisms like timer interrupts or system calls that force the CPU to stop the current task and jump to the scheduler. Without those, the OS would have to wait for the process to finish on its own, which defeats multitasking. Here is a tiny program that pretends to be the OS timer. It counts down and, when the counter reaches zero, prints a message saying the scheduler would take over. Now picture the flow of control as the OS steps in, saves the current state, chooses the next process, and restores its state. The OS must use privileged actions to interrupt and switch processes. Try writing a loop that prints a message every second and then stops.

while counter:
    time.sleep(1)
    counter -= 1
